title: Characterization of Thermophilic Cellulases from Talaromyces leycettanus and Their Synergistic Action
author: Yuan Gu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8g4htyw
materials: Purification of recombinant Tl Cel5A and Tl Cel6A
Fractions showing cellulase activities were pooled and further desalted with a 5 kDa molecular cut-off concentration tube (Millipore) using 0.1 M McIlvaine buffer (pH 3.5 or 4.5).
Residual activities were determined as described above.

steps.title: Amplify cellulase genes by PCR
steps.instruction: Amplify the full‑length cellulase‑encoding genes Tlcel5A and Tlcel6A from T. leycettanus genomic DNA using primers GH5F/GH5R and GH6F/GH6R. Run PCR at 95 °C for 3 min, then 30 cycles of 95 °C for 30 s, 60 °C for 60 s, and 72 °C for 1 min.

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA and amplify mature coding regions
steps.instruction: Synthesize cDNA in vitro with the ReverTra Ace‑a™ kit, then amplify the mature coding sequences of Tl Cel5A and Tl Cel6A using primers GH5F1/GH5R1 and GH6F1/GH6R1 that contain appropriate restriction sites.

steps.title: Clone PCR products into pGEM‑T Easy
steps.instruction: Ligate the PCR products into the pGEM‑T Easy vector, transform the ligation mixture into E. coli Trans1‑T1 cells, and plate on selective medium.

steps.title: Subclone mature cDNA into Pichia expression vector
steps.instruction: Digest the cDNA fragments with SnaBI (or EcoRI) and NotI, ligate them into the pPIC9 vector to generate pPIC9‑Tlcel5A and pPIC9‑Tlcel6A expression constructs.

steps.title: Linearize plasmids and transform Pichia
steps.instruction: Linearize each recombinant plasmid with BglII, then introduce the linear DNA into P. pastoris GS115 competent cells by electroporation.

steps.title: Select transformants and perform small‑scale expression
steps.instruction: Plate electroporated cells on MD agar plates, pick positive colonies into 10 mL tubes containing 3 mL BMGY and grow for 2 days at 30 °C, 220 rpm; then replace medium with 1 mL BMMY and continue for another 2 days under the same conditions.

steps.title: Large‑scale expression in shake flasks
steps.instruction: Inoculate the most active transformants into 1 L shake flasks containing 400 mL BMGY; incubate at 30 °C, 220 rpm for 2 days. Pellet cells by centrifugation, resuspend the pellet in 200 mL BMMY and grow for 3 days at 30 °C, 200 rpm, adding methanol to a final concentration of 0.5 % every 24 h for induction.

steps.title: Harvest culture supernatants
steps.instruction: Collect the supernatants by centrifugation at 5 000 rpm for 10 min (initial harvest) or at 4500×g for further processing, and keep at 4 °C until purification.

steps.title: Concentrate and buffer‑exchange enzymes
steps.instruction: Use a VivaFlow 200 ultrafiltration system with a 5 kDa cut‑off membrane to concentrate the crude enzymes and exchange the buffer to 0.1 M Tris‑HCl, pH 8.0.

steps.title: Desalt and purify recombinant proteins
steps.instruction: Pass the concentrated sample through a HiTrap™ Desalting column for desalting, then load onto a pre‑equilibrated HiTrap Q Sepharose XL FPLC column (0.1 M Tris‑HCl, pH 8.0). Elute proteins with a linear NaCl gradient from 0 to 0.7 M at a flow rate of 3 mL/min.

steps.title: Assess purity and determine concentration
steps.instruction: Run the purified proteins on a 12 % SDS‑PAGE gel to evaluate purity and molecular mass; measure protein concentration using the Bradford assay.

steps.title: Deglycosylate purified enzymes
steps.instruction: Treat the purified Tl Cel5A and Tl Cel6A with Endo H (New England Biolabs) for 2 h at 37 °C according to the manufacturer’s protocol, then verify deglycosylation by SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: Prepare standard cellulase activity assay
steps.instruction: Mix 100 µL of appropriately diluted enzyme with 900 µL of 1 % (w/v) substrate solution (CMC‑Na, barley β‑glucan or lichenan) in 0.1 M McIlvaine buffer (pH 3.5 or 4.5). Incubate at 75 °C for Tl Cel5A or 80 °C for Tl Cel6A for 10 min (use 5 mg/mL Avicel and incubate 60 min). Stop the reaction and determine reducing sugars by the DNS method. Define one unit (U) as the amount of enzyme that releases 1 µmol reducing sugar per minute.

steps.title: Determine optimal pH
steps.instruction: Assay enzyme activity at 75 °C (Tl Cel5A) or 80 °C (Tl Cel6A) in 0.1 M McIlvaine buffer across pH 2.0–8.0 to find the pH giving maximal activity.

steps.title: Assess pH stability
steps.instruction: Pre‑incubate purified enzymes at 37 °C for 60 min in buffers covering pH 1.0–12.0 (0.1 M KCl‑HCl for pH 1.0–2.0, 0.1 M McIlvaine for pH 2.0–8.0, 0.1 M glycine‑NaOH for pH 9.0–12.0). After incubation, measure residual activity at 75 °C, pH 3.5 for Tl Cel5A and at 80 °C (barley β‑glucan) or 70 °C (PASC), pH 4.5 for Tl Cel6A.

steps.title: Determine optimal temperature
steps.instruction: Perform the standard activity assay at temperatures ranging from 30 °C to 90 °C (10 min incubation) at pH 3.5 for Tl Cel5A or pH 4.5 for Tl Cel6A to locate the temperature of maximal activity.

steps.title: Evaluate thermal stability
steps.instruction: Incubate each enzyme at 70 °C, 75 °C or 80 °C in the appropriate pH buffer (3.5 for Cel5A, 4.5 for Cel6A) for various time periods, then assay residual activity under standard conditions.

steps.title: Determine enzyme half‑life
steps.instruction: Incubate 0.05 mg of Tl Cel5A or 0.2 mg of Tl Cel6A at 60 °C, 65 °C or 70 °C for 0.5–24 h; after each time point, measure remaining activity to calculate half‑life.

steps.title: Test substrate specificity
steps.instruction: Measure activity (using the DNS assay) on 1 % (w/v) of each substrate: CMC‑Na, barley β‑glucan, Avicel, lichenan, laminarin, xyloglucan, birchwood xylan, konjac flour, locust bean gum, glucomannan, and on 0.2 mM p‑NPGlu, p‑NPGal, p‑NPC.

steps.title: Determine kinetic parameters for Cel5A
steps.instruction: Incubate Tl Cel5A with CMC‑Na concentrations ranging from 0.25 to 10 mg/mL at pH 3.5 and 75 °C for 5 min. Calculate Km, Vmax and kcat/Km from Lineweaver‑Burk plots using GraphPad Prism 6.0.

steps.title: Determine kinetic parameters for Cel6A
steps.instruction: Incubate Tl Cel6A with barley β‑glucan concentrations of 0.25–10 mg/mL at pH 4.5 and 80 °C for 5 min. Determine Km, Vmax and kcat/Km as above.

steps.title: Analyze hydrolysis products by HPAEC
steps.instruction: Add 0.05 U Tl Cel5A or 0.02 U Tl Cel6A to 1 mL of 200 µg mL⁻¹ cellotetraose, cellopentaose or cellohexaose. Incubate at 60 °C for 0, 1, 5, 30, 60, 240 or 300 min. Stop reactions by boiling, dilute samples 100‑fold with ddH₂O, inject 100 µL into a Dionex HPAEC (model 2500) using 100 mM NaOH as eluent. Identify peaks with standards of glucose, cellobiose, cellotriose, cellotetraose, cellopentaose, and cellohexaose; calculate product amounts from peak areas.

steps.title: Synergistic hydrolysis with Avicel
steps.instruction: Prepare enzyme mixtures at total enzyme concentration 4.0 mM with the following Tl Cel5A:Tl Cel6A ratios: 0.4:3.6, 0.8:3.2, 1.2:2.8, 1.6:2.4, 2.0:2.0, 2.4:1.6, 2.8:1.2, 3.2:0.8, 3.6:0.4. Add each mixture to 5 mg/mL Avicel in 50 mM McIlvaine buffer, pH 4.0, and incubate at 60 °C for 24 h. Determine released reducing sugars by the DNS method.

steps.title: Synergistic hydrolysis with SECS or Avicel
steps.instruction: Incubate 8 µM of either Tl Cel5A or Tl Cel6A alone, or 4 µM of each enzyme together, with 5 mg/mL SECS or Avicel in 0.1 M McIlvaine buffer, pH 4.0, at 60 °C for 12 h or 18 h. Measure reducing sugars by DNS.

steps.title: Synergistic hydrolysis with PASC
steps.instruction: Add 2 µM of a single enzyme or 1 µM each of Tl Cel5A and Tl Cel6A to 2.5 mg/mL PASC in 0.1 M McIlvaine buffer, pH 4.0, and incubate at 60 °C (time not specified). Determine reducing sugars by DNS.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of synergistic effects
steps.instruction: Analyze the glucose‑release data using one‑factor ANOVA in SPSS 19.0; consider differences significant at P < 0.05.
